### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-06 06:54

Because your app only requests basic scopes (email + profile), this is quick — Google **doesn't force verification** for non-sensitive scopes, so publishing takes effect immediately and any Google account can sign in. (Note: Google recently renamed this area from "OAuth consent screen" to **Google Auth Platform**, so I'll give both paths.)

**1. Open the right project.** Go to [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com), and in the project picker at the top select the project that holds your Locare OAuth client (the one with `Client ID` = your `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`).

**2. Go to the consent/audience settings.**
- New UI: left menu → **Google Auth Platform** → **Audience**.
- Older UI: **APIs & Services** → **OAuth consent screen**.

**3. Make sure the basics are filled** (publishing is blocked otherwise). On the **Branding** page (or the consent screen form) confirm:
- **App name** (e.g. "Locare")
- **User support email**
- **Developer contact email**
- **User type: External** (this is what lets non-org Google accounts in)

A homepage/privacy-policy link is only *required* for verification (sensitive scopes), which you don't need — but filling them is good practice.

**4. Publish.** On the **Audience** page you'll see **Publishing status: Testing**. Click **Publish app**, then confirm the "Push to production?" dialog. The status changes to **In production**.

**That's it.** Because you're only using `email`/`profile`/`openid`, there's no verification review to wait on — any Google account can now complete "Continue with Google" at `app.locare.co.za`. They still only get *access* if their email has a role (otherwise they hit `/no-access`), so opening authentication up is safe.

Two things to know:
- You can **remove the test-user list** now — it's ignored in production.
- If you ever add **sensitive scopes** later (e.g. reading Gmail/Drive), *then* Google requires the full verification process (domain ownership, privacy policy, security review). For login-only, you'll never hit that.

Once it's published, try signing in with a fresh Google account that you've given a role — it should go straight through without the "app isn't verified" screen.

Sources:
- [Manage App Audience — Google Cloud Help](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945?hl=en)
- [Manage OAuth App Branding — Google Cloud Help](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549049?hl=en)
- [Configure the OAuth consent screen — Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/configure-oauth-consent)

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-06 07:19

Create a **new, separate TXT record** — do **not** modify the existing one.

Your apex already has a TXT record for SPF (`v=spf1 +a +mx +include:spf.host-ww.net …`). A domain can hold **multiple TXT records on the same name**, and they're independent. If you paste the Google string *into* the SPF record you'll break email authentication — so leave SPF exactly as it is and add a second TXT alongside it.

At HostAfrica (DNS Management → **+ Add DNS Record**):

- **Type:** TXT
- **Name / Host:** `@` (the apex — same as your SPF record; some panels want it blank or `locare.co.za`)
- **RDATA / Value:** `google-site-verification=DizSDIdL8PlUZ167kAn36T2DRHSG9CB15p0wXU14tkQ`
- **TTL:** default (3600 is fine)

Save it, wait a few minutes for propagation, then press **Verify** in Google. You can confirm it's live from your PC first:

```
nslookup -type=txt locare.co.za
```

You should see **two** TXT entries — your existing `v=spf1…` and the new `google-site-verification=…`. If it doesn't verify immediately, give it up to an hour (occasionally longer) and retry; the record is correct as long as both TXT values show up.

One note: HostAfrica displayed your SPF record wrapped in quotes in the panel earlier, so if it auto-adds quotes, that's fine — just make sure the value between them is exactly the `google-site-verification=…` string with nothing extra.

Two of the three are homepage issues I've now fixed; the third is a Google Cloud console setting. Deploy the marketing site:

```
git add -A && git commit -m "fix(marketing): always-visible hero purpose + Locare name for Google brand verification" && git push
git pull   # on the VPS
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env.prod -f deploy/compose.prod.yml up -d --build marketing
```

Mapping each of Google's three complaints:

**1. "Home page does not explain the purpose"** — fixed. The hero now states it plainly and *always visibly* (no longer hidden behind the scroll animation): *"Locare is a white-label property-management platform for South African rental agencies… leasing, rent collection, trust accounting, owner payouts, maintenance, and branded tenant & landlord apps."*

**2. "App name doesn't match the home page"** — fixed. "Locare" is now in the H1 headline as real text (was only in an image logo before), plus the title, meta description, and body. Make sure the consent screen's **App name is exactly `Locare`** (Google Auth Platform → Branding) so they match.

**3. "Logo does not uniquely identify your brand"** — this one is **in Google Cloud, not the site.** In **Google Auth Platform → Branding → App logo**, upload *your own* Locare logo:
- Use the actual Locare mark (you have `marketing/locare-logo.png` / the SVGs in `marketing/brand/`).
- It must be **square** (120×120 px), PNG/JPG, under 1 MB — if your logo is a wide wordmark, export just the square mark/icon version.
- It must be genuinely your brand and not resemble another company's logo (that's what "impersonate" means). The real Locare logo passes; a placeholder or stock icon fails.

Then in the same Branding section confirm **App home page = `https://locare.co.za`** and the authorized domain is `locare.co.za`.

After the marketing site redeploys and you've set the consent-screen app name + uploaded the square Locare logo, **re-submit for verification.** Google re-crawls the homepage; with the purpose and name now visible as text, complaints 1 and 2 should clear, and the proper logo clears 3.

One tip: after deploying, open `https://locare.co.za` in a private window and confirm the "Locare is a white-label property-management platform…" line is visible immediately on load (not fading in) — that's what the crawler needs to see.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-06 07:51

First pass done on the marketing site — the highest-impact public page. Changes:

- **Fixed a real bug in font loading.** The `preconnect` hints pointed at Google Fonts, but your fonts come from **Fontshare** — so the early-connection was wasted. Now it preconnects to the actual font hosts (`api.fontshare.com` / `cdn.fontshare.com`).
- **Made fonts non-render-blocking.** The Fontshare stylesheet was blocking first paint; it now loads async (`preload → stylesheet`) with a `<noscript>` fallback, and `display=swap` keeps text visible immediately. Faster first paint / better LCP.
- **Long-lived cache headers.** Static assets (SVG/PNG/CSS/JS/woff2) now get a 30-day `Cache-Control`, while HTML stays fresh with a short must-revalidate — so repeat visits are near-instant without serving stale pages.
- (The earlier hero fix — content no longer hidden behind the scroll animation — also improves perceived load.)

Good news from the audit: no heavy images (all logos are small SVGs) and **no third-party JavaScript** at all, so those common bottlenecks don't apply here.

Deploy the marketing container:

```
git add -A && git commit -m "perf(marketing): fix font preconnect, async font load, static cache headers" && git push
git pull   # on the VPS
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env.prod -f deploy/compose.prod.yml up -d --build marketing
```

**What's left on #213** needs the build environment, which is currently unavailable to me here: a **Lighthouse measurement** (to quantify before/after) and the **web-admin (Next.js) bundle pass** — analyzing the JS bundle, code-splitting heavy routes (e.g. the recharts Reports page), and lazy-loading. I can do those when the sandbox is back, or you can run `npx lighthouse https://locare.co.za` and a `next build` bundle report and paste the results — I'll optimize against the actual numbers.

The app can send a message "successfully" at the SMTP layer, but if the mailbox's inbound routing is broken it'll never land — and a Gmail test proves that independently of the app.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-06 15:50

That error is the smoking gun, and it's good news — **the app is reaching HostAfrica's mail server and authenticating; only the TLS certificate name doesn't match.** You're connecting to `mail.locare.co.za`, but the server presents a certificate for its real hostname, **`da30.host-ww.net`**, so Node's TLS check rejects it.

The fix is a one-line env change: connect using the server's actual certificate hostname instead of the friendly alias. In `deploy/.env.prod`:

```
SMTP_HOST=da30.host-ww.net
```

(Leave everything else the same — `SMTP_PORT=465`, `SMTP_USER=partners@locare.co.za`, the password, and `SMTP_FROM=partners@locare.co.za`. Your mailbox lives on that server, so auth still works; you're just pointing at the name the cert is actually issued for.)

Then recreate the api container so it picks up the new env (no rebuild needed):

```
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env.prod -f deploy/compose.prod.yml up -d --force-recreate api
```

Submit another application and re-check:

```
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env.prod -f deploy/compose.prod.yml logs --tail=40 api | grep -iE "email sent|email .* failed"
```

You should now see `email sent → partners@locare.co.za via SmtpEmailProvider (…)` and the mail should land in the inbox (it's the same server delivering to its own mailbox).

If you'd rather keep the friendly `mail.locare.co.za` name (in case HostAfrica ever moves you off `da30`), tell me and I'll add an `SMTP_SERVERNAME` option to the provider so TLS verifies against the cert host while still connecting to the alias — but the `da30.host-ww.net` change above is the standard HostAfrica setup and gets you working right now. Paste the log line after you retry.

Done. Both app hosts in `deploy/Caddyfile` now serve the HTML document with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (browser must revalidate on every load) while `/_next/static/*` and `/brand/*` stay hard-cached as immutable. This is the durable fix: after any future deploy, browsers pick up the new HTML → new chunk hashes → correct branding, instead of replaying a stale page.

To apply it and clear the current stale cache:

```bash
cd ~/PMS0.3 && git pull
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
```

(If `reload` complains, `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml restart caddy` works too — the Caddyfile is mounted, no rebuild needed.)

One catch: the HTML already sitting in your phone/desktop cache was stored under the *old* cacheable header, so it won't revalidate on its own. You need to hard-clear cache **once** on each device you've already visited from:

- **Phone (Chrome):** ⋮ → History → Clear browsing data → Cached images and files.
- **Desktop:** DevTools open → right-click reload → "Empty Cache and Hard Reload".

After that one clear, `no-cache` keeps every device current automatically going forward.

When you reload app.locare.co.za post-clear, F12 console should now print the `[brand]` line with `isPlatformHost: true` — that confirms the new bundle loaded and Locare branding is resolving. Paste it here and I'll remove the temporary debug log.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-06 18:51

Typecheck passes clean. Fixed at the source — here's what was actually wrong:

`brandKey()` reads `window.location.hostname`, which doesn't exist during server render, so it fell back to the Dantalan vendor slug and rendered `DEFAULT_BRANDING` — literally the string "Property Manager". Next then **statically prerendered** that HTML at build time (that's the `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` and the `s-maxage` we kept fighting) and served the same baked file to every host. The Locare card looked right only because the client-side effect corrected it after hydration; the shell and `<title>` did not.

Four changes:

- **`lib/brand-shared.ts`** (new) — brand constants + `brandKeyFromHost(host)` with no `'use client'`, so server code can use them.
- **`app/layout.tsx`** — reads the `Host` header, resolves the brand server-side, and sets `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` so the HTML is never prerendered with one host's brand.
- **`components/brand-provider.tsx`** — seeds from that server brand (no flash), debug log removed.
- **`components/shell.tsx`** — the authed shell no longer server-renders, which kills the "Property Manager" sidebar that flashed on `/` before the redirect to `/login`.

Commit and push from **Windows**:
```
git add web-admin/lib/brand-shared.ts web-admin/lib/branding.ts web-admin/app/layout.tsx web-admin/components/brand-provider.tsx web-admin/components/shell.tsx
git commit -m "fix(web): resolve brand from Host header server-side; stop prerendering wrong brand"
git push origin main
```

Then on the **VPS** (from the repo root, so compose finds the env):
```bash
cd ~/PMS03 && git pull
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod build web
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod up -d --force-recreate web
```

The rebuild is required — this is a server-render change, so it must be baked into a new image. After it's up, `app.locare.co.za` will serve Locare branding in the HTML itself, on first paint, for every visitor regardless of cache.

To a reviewer that's an app with a different name and no stated purpose — exactly the two things they flagged.

Two fixes:

- **`app/layout.tsx`** — `generateMetadata()` now derives title/description/og from the host, so the page is `Locare — Back-office` with a real description instead of the generic "Back-office".
- **`components/shell.tsx`** — the pre-hydration state renders a branded splash (name, tagline, one-line purpose) instead of nothing, so there's always crawlable content.

Commit, push, and rebuild web:
```powershell
git add web-admin/app/layout.tsx web-admin/components/shell.tsx
git commit -m "fix(web): brand-aware metadata + crawlable splash for OAuth brand verification"
git push origin main
```
```bash
cd ~/PMS03 && git pull
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod build web
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod up -d --force-recreate web
```

Before you resubmit, confirm in the Google Cloud console that **App name** is exactly `Locare` (not "Locare Back-office" or a project name) and **Application home page** is `https://locare.co.za` — the name must match the H1 on that page verbatim. Then resubmit; each rejection is scored against a fresh crawl, so the earlier failures don't carry over.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-07 09:25

Done. Partner registration is now two stages.

**Stage 1** (`/partner-apply`) asks three things — name, email, mobile — then shows a "check your email" confirmation. No ID numbers, no directors, no banking, no documents. The link is only ever emailed, never returned to the browser, so opening it also verifies the address before you collect any PII.

**Stage 2** (`/partner-apply/continue?id=…&token=…`) holds the individual/business choice, KYC/KYB fields, banking, consent and document uploads. Every step saves server-side before advancing, so someone who wanders off to find their bank confirmation letter can reopen the same link and resume exactly where they were — the old form lost everything on refresh. Links last **14 days**, and an expired one offers a self-serve "email me a new link" button.

Behind that: leads land in the admin queue as **Started** with a "Resend link" action, `partners@locare.co.za` gets a new-enquiry notification, and an hourly job sends **one** reminder to anyone who hasn't finished after 48h (`reminder_sent_at` guarantees it never repeats).

Two notes worth flagging:

- There's a new migration (`1720000038000-PartnerApplicationReminder`) — it needs to run on deploy.
- I kept the old single-shot `create()` service method and its `POST` shape intact for API compatibility, but the public route now points at the two-stage flow.

New env knobs, both optional: `PARTNER_APP_LINK_DAYS` (14) and `PARTNER_APP_REMINDER_HOURS` (48).

To ship it — commit and push from Windows, then on the VPS rebuild `api` and `web` and run migrations. Worth testing with a real address first: submit stage 1, confirm the email arrives, and walk the link through to submit.

That's the design working as intended — nothing is pending approval yet.

Your lead is sitting in the **Started** status: contact details captured, KYC link emailed, but the vetting isn't done. The admin queue defaults to the **Submitted** filter, so click the **Started** chip on `Admin → Partner applications` and you'll see it, with the contact's name, email, phone and a *Resend link* button.

It only moves into the approval queue once they open the emailed link and complete stage 2 — choose individual/business, fill in KYC/KYB and banking, upload the required documents, and hit Submit. At that point it flips to **Submitted** with a *Review →* action, and approving it provisions the partner and their login as before.

Worth walking your own test application all the way through to Submit to confirm the full path, since that's the part that hasn't been exercised live yet.

Run these two on the VPS:

```bash
cd ~/PMS03
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod exec api printenv PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS
grep -n PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS deploy/.env.prod
```

Three likely outcomes:

- **Empty / not set in the container** — the var isn't reaching the API. Add it to `deploy/.env.prod`, and check `compose.prod.yml`'s `api.environment` block actually passes it through.
- **Set, but doesn't contain your address** — add it. Comma-separated, no spaces needed: `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=ahjones101@gmail.com,you@locare.co.za`
- **Looks correct** — then it's a mismatch between that value and the address you signed in with. Comparison is lowercased and trimmed on both sides, so watch for a different address than you expect (e.g. you signed in with a Google account on a different address than the one listed).

After editing `.env.prod`, the API must be recreated to pick it up — a restart alone won't re-read the env file:

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod up -d --force-recreate api
```

Then sign out on your phone and sign in again — the role is baked into the JWT at login, so an existing session keeps the old (no-access) claims until you get a fresh token.

Right now Custom is the fourth equal column, which works against you twice: it squeezes the three *real* tiers into narrow cards, and it puts a price-less "Talk to us" next to hard numbers, so the eye reads it as the runt of the set rather than the premium option.

Some directions worth considering:

**Three across, Custom as a full-width band below.** The three priced tiers get ~33% wider each (better feature-list readability), and Custom becomes a horizontal strip — copy left, CTA right. This is the pattern Stripe/Linear/Vercel converged on, because "enterprise" genuinely *is* a different kind of thing, not a bigger version of the same thing.

**Three across, Custom offset right.** Same three-card row, then Custom deliberately misaligned below — narrower, pushed to the right column, whitespace to its left. Editorial and more distinctive, closest to what you described. Needs care at tablet width.

**Asymmetric bento.** Growth doubles in size as the hero, others tuck around it. Visually interesting but it makes tier comparison harder, which is the one job a pricing table has.

**Custom as a one-line footnote.** Just "Bigger portfolio, or something unusual? Talk to us →" under the grid. Maximum restraint, but you lose the feature list that helps sell bespoke work.

My instinct is the first or second — both fix the width problem, and both stop Custom competing on price. Let me pin down which:

Honest read, grouped by how much they'd hurt you:

**Would embarrass you today**

- **Your privacy policy and terms still have fill-in-the-blanks.** 11 placeholders live right now — `[Legal entity name]` ×5, `[registered address]` ×3, `[reg no.]`, `[DATE]` ×2. Those pages are public, linked from the footer and the apps, and Google's reviewer is crawling that domain. Fastest thing on this list to fix.
- **Google OAuth is still unverified**, so "Continue with Google" shows real users the scary unverified-app screen.

**Blocking a first paying customer**

- **WhatsApp isn't live** (#204). It's the headline of the design — WhatsApp-primary onboarding — but the channel is off, so everything silently falls back to email. Until the Meta business account exists, that feature doesn't exist.
- **No rand has ever moved through the system** (#126). Six gateways integrated, none proven. iKhokha callback verification is still in monitor mode, not enforce.
- **Subscription billing has never charged anyone.** You built recurring agency billing and pricing tiers; no agency has been billed, so the revenue path is entirely untested.
- **Self-serve signup → pay → provision has never been walked by a stranger.** You've only ever provisioned agencies yourself.

**Operational risk**

- **Backups may not be running.** `deploy/backup.sh` exists but its header says "add to cron" — worth confirming it's actually scheduled, and doing one restore test. An untested backup isn't a backup.
- **Nothing is watching production.** No error tracking, no uptime monitoring, no alerting. If the API dies at 2am, a tenant tells you.
- **Deploy is fragile.** Today's stale `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS` proved env drift between root `.env` and `deploy/.env.prod`. One deploy script would remove a whole class of "why isn't my change live" debugging.

**Product maturity**

- Mobile apps are Expo web exports on subdomains — not in the App Store or Play Store.
- Multi-tenancy is enforced in the database but has never run with two live agencies at once.
- Lease parser is unshipped pending the Anthropic key (#152).

If I were picking the order: legal text (30 minutes), then backups + monitoring (they protect everything else), then WhatsApp, then a real R1 test payment.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-11 16:05

Only **two** are strictly required to switch WhatsApp on:

```bash
WHATSAPP_TOKEN=            # permanent access token (System User token)
WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID=         # the sender's Phone Number ID (numeric, not the phone number)
```

The provider registry checks exactly those two — if either is missing, WhatsApp stays `off` and the cascade silently falls through to email. That's the switch.

The rest have working defaults, but you'll want to set them explicitly:

```bash
WHATSAPP_OTP_TEMPLATE=locare_otp          # approved AUTHENTICATION template
WHATSAPP_WELCOME_TEMPLATE=locare_welcome  # approved UTILITY template
WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANG=en                 # must match the template's language exactly
OTP_CHANNELS=whatsapp,email               # already set — cascade order
WELCOME_CHANNELS=                         # optional; falls back to OTP_CHANNELS
```

Where each value comes from in Meta:

- **WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID** — Business Manager → WhatsApp Manager → API Setup. It's the "Phone number ID" field, a long number. Not `+27…`.
- **WHATSAPP_TOKEN** — do *not* use the temporary 24-hour token from the API Setup page. Create a System User under Business Settings → Users → System Users, give it Admin access to the WhatsApp Business Account, then generate a token with the `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management` scopes and set expiry to **Never**. A 24-hour token means WhatsApp dies silently tomorrow and every OTP quietly falls back to email.

Two things that will bite you regardless of the env vars:

**Templates must be approved before anything sends.** The OTP one must be created with category **Authentication** and include a copy-code button — the provider sends a `copy_code` button component, and it'll fail if the template doesn't have one. Body placeholder is `{{1}}` (the code). The welcome template is **Utility** with `{{1}}` = first name, `{{2}}` = agency name. Approval usually takes minutes but can take a day.

**The template names in your env must match Meta exactly**, including language code. `en` and `en_US` are different templates as far as the API is concerned.

Once set, recreate the API container and check the boot log:

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod up -d --force-recreate api
docker compose -f deploy/compose.prod.yml --env-file deploy/.env.prod logs --tail=50 api | grep "channels —"
```

You want `whatsapp:WhatsAppCloudProvider` rather than `whatsapp:off`. Then request an OTP to your own number to confirm delivery end to end.

Full setup walkthrough is in `docs/LOCARE_WHATSAPP_ONBOARDING_DESIGN.md` §8 if you want the Meta-side detail.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-11 16:12

They're not values you fetch — **you create the templates and you choose the names.** The env vars just have to match what you named them in Meta.

**Where:** Meta Business Suite → WhatsApp Manager → **Message Templates** → *Create template*. Nothing exists until you make it.

**Template 1 — the OTP**

- Name: `locare_otp` (lowercase, underscores only — that string is what goes in the env var)
- Category: **Authentication**
- Language: English
- Body: *Your Locare verification code is {{1}}. It expires in 10 minutes.*
- Button: **Copy code** (Meta's one-time-code button)

The copy-code button is not optional. The provider always sends a `copy_code` button component for auth templates, so a template without one gets rejected by the API at send time.

**Template 2 — the tenant welcome**

- Name: `locare_welcome`
- Category: **Utility**
- Language: English
- Body: *Hi {{1}}, your {{2}} tenant account is ready. Open the app to view your lease, pay rent and log maintenance: https://app.locare.co.za*

`{{1}}` is the first name and `{{2}}` the agency name — that's the order the code passes them in, so don't swap them.

**WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANG** is the language code Meta assigns when you pick a language. Choose plain "English" and it's `en`; "English (US)" gives you `en_US`. Whichever you pick, copy it exactly — Meta treats them as different templates and a mismatch fails the send.

Approval is free and usually takes minutes to a few hours; Authentication templates are near-instant since the format is standardised.

One sequencing note: leave `WHATSAPP_TOKEN` blank until both templates show **Approved**. The cascade runs email-only in the meantime and nothing breaks — whereas setting the token with unapproved templates means every OTP fails its first hop before falling back.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-11 16:24

No — and there's a real bug hiding in that question.

**Email OTP** (from `auth.service.ts`, sent as subject *"Your sign-in code"*):

> Your one-time sign-in code is `123456`. It expires in **5 minutes**. If you didn't request it, ignore this message.

The "5" isn't hardcoded — it's `OTP_TTL_SECONDS / 60`, and your `.env` has `OTP_TTL_SECONDS=300`.

**The WhatsApp template in my design doc** says *"It expires in 10 minutes."* That's wrong. A tenant getting the WhatsApp version would be told 10 minutes for a code that dies at 5. Change it to 5 when you create the template — or if you'd rather give people longer, bump `OTP_TTL_SECONDS` to 600 and leave the template at 10.

Also worth knowing before you sit down in WhatsApp Manager: **you can't write custom copy for Authentication templates.** Meta fixes the body to a standard form — `{{1}} is your verification code.` — and you only get to toggle add-ons:

- "For your security, do not share this code." (security disclaimer)
- "This code expires in N minutes." (expiry warning — you set N as a fixed number on the template, not a variable)

So the doc's wording was aspirational. What you'll actually produce is roughly:

> **123456** is your verification code. For your security, do not share this code. This code expires in 5 minutes.
> `[Copy code]`

Which is close enough in substance to the email, just phrased Meta's way. The one thing you must get right is **N = 5**, matching `OTP_TTL_SECONDS`.

One consequence of the fixed format: if you later change `OTP_TTL_SECONDS`, the email text updates automatically but the WhatsApp template does not — it needs re-submitting to Meta. Worth a comment in `.env.prod` next to that variable.

Want me to correct the design doc and add that warning comment?

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 05:48

Grounded picture first, because you've got more scaffolding than you might realise — and one significant hole.

**What exists:** a `leads` table capturing name/email/phone/company/message from the marketing form and the chatbot, and an email notification to `LEADS_NOTIFY_EMAIL`. The site chatbot is Phase 1 — scripted keyword matching, with a `/api/faq-chat` hook already stubbed for Phase 2. The partner programme gives you a commissioned human sales channel.

**The hole:** there's no leads admin UI, no pipeline, no follow-up. A lead arrives, an email fires, and then nothing. No status, no reminder, no second touch. That matters because it changes what "sales agent" should mean for you.

Four directions:

**1. Site agent (inbound conversion).** Finish Phase 2 — swap keyword matching for a real agent that answers from your actual content, qualifies by portfolio size, recommends the right tier, and captures the lead *with* that qualification attached. Converts traffic you're already generating. Uses the same Anthropic key you need for the lease parser anyway.

**2. Nurture agent (the leaky bucket).** A lead pipeline in the back-office plus sequenced automated follow-up over email and WhatsApp — day 0, day 2, day 7 — that stops when they reply. This is where deals actually die for solo founders. Unglamorous, highest yield.

**3. Prospecting agent (outbound).** Research SA rental agencies, enrich, draft personalised outreach for your review.

⚠️ Worth being blunt here: **POPIA section 69** restricts unsolicited electronic direct marketing to prior consent, and South Africa unusually treats juristic persons as data subjects too — so B2B cold email isn't the free pass it is in the US. You're selling POPIA-aligned software; getting caught spamming would be a genuinely bad look. A research-and-draft agent where *you* choose the channel (phone, LinkedIn, in-person) is defensible. An automated cold-email cannon is not.

**4. Partner enablement.** Arm your partners with pitch material and nudge their stale referrals — leverages the commission machinery you've already built.

My honest read: **2, then 1.** Pointing an agent at generating more leads before anything catches them is pouring water into a bucket with no bottom. Fix the bucket, then turn on the tap.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 05:54

**First, a problem:** you have no `robots.txt`, no `sitemap.xml`, no canonical tags and no structured data. Google is crawling a single-page site with nothing telling it what else exists. That's an hour of work and it gates everything else — no point publishing content into a site search engines can't map.

Then, the agent options ranked by how well they fit *your* situation:

**Content agent — the compounding play.** Weekly: pick something SA rental agencies actually search for, draft a genuinely useful piece, publish it as a static page under `/guides`, update the sitemap. Your unfair advantage is real here — you know PPRA trust accounting, POPIA obligations for landlords, deposit interest rules, the PIE Act eviction process. Most SA competitors publish thin marketing fluff. One good piece a week beats five thin ones; the agent drafts, you edit.

**Free tools — link-bait that converts.** Rental escalation calculator. Deposit interest calculator (SA law requires you pay tenants interest — agencies get this wrong constantly). Commission calculator. Rent-to-income affordability check. These rank for long-tail queries, attract links, and catch someone mid-task who has the exact problem you solve. An agent can build and maintain one per fortnight.

**Distribution agent.** Researches and drafts submissions for Capterra, GetApp, Software Advice, SaaSHub, Product Hunt, SA business directories, property industry bodies. Mostly one-off, front-loaded value, and you'll need to press submit yourself on most.

**The rentals-site flywheel — highest ceiling.** You already generate branded listing sites per agency. Every listing page is indexable. A tasteful "Powered by Locare" footer link turns each agency's listing traffic into backlinks and referrals — this is how Calendly and Shopify actually grew. Costs nothing per agency and compounds. Needs customers first, but worth designing in now so it's there from agency one.

**Social/community.** Drafts LinkedIn posts and comments for SA property groups. Honest caveat: an agent posting into communities gets sniffed out fast. Works as a drafting aid for your voice, not as autopilot.

The good news is I can build any of these as a scheduled agent — same mechanism as your Monday review — so it runs weekly without you thinking about it.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 06:09

All four built.

**SEO foundations** — `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, canonical tags on every page, and a JSON-LD graph (Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication with your three price tiers, plus FAQPage mirroring the nine visible FAQs). The FAQ schema is the sleeper here: it's what Google shows as rich results and what AI assistants quote when someone asks about SA property software.

**Four calculators** at `/tools` — rental escalation, deposit interest, agency commission, rent affordability. Each is a separate indexable page with its own schema, 200–300 words of genuine explanation beneath the tool, and a CTA. They're not toys: the deposit one covers the Rental Housing Act s5 obligation most agencies get wrong, and the affordability one subtracts existing debt rather than blindly applying the 30% rule.

**Powered-by flywheel** — quiet attribution in the rentals footer and the public chrome footer, suppressed on Locare's own host so it isn't circular. Every listing page an agency publishes now links back.

**Weekly content agent** — Tuesdays 07:00. It picks an unwritten topic from a priority list, **searches the web to verify legal specifics before writing** (I was explicit that it must not invent section numbers), writes 900–1,500 words into `marketing/guides/`, updates the guides index and sitemap, then reports to you with the commands to publish. It won't commit or deploy anything itself.

```powershell
git add marketing web-admin/components/public-chrome.tsx web-admin/app/rentals/page.tsx
git commit -m "growth: SEO foundations, free calculators, guides section, powered-by attribution"
```

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 11:36

Worth being clear on what I can actually produce: I can't render video, but I can give you everything up to the render — script with timings, shot-by-shot click paths through your real product, on-screen caption copy, and animated HTML title/outro cards you screen-record at 1080p. You'd do the capture in OBS or ScreenPal (both free) and assemble in CapCut or DaVinci Resolve.

One thing to flag before anything else: **you'd be filming Dantalan's live data.** Real tenant names, phone numbers, ID numbers, banking details. Seed a demo agency with fictional data first — a POPIA breach in your own promo video for POPIA-aligned software would be a bad day.

Concepts worth considering:

**"Month-end in sixty seconds."** Follow one rent cycle end to end — invoice generates, tenant pays on their phone, payment auto-reconciles against the ledger, owner statement builds itself, payout splits. This is the strongest option because month-end is the pain every agency owner feels physically, and it shows the double-entry engine that actually differentiates you from the spreadsheet crowd.

**"Your brand, not ours."** The same screens flipping through three different agency identities — logo, colours, domain — in a few seconds. Visually arresting and it lands the white-label pitch faster than any sentence could. Weaker as a standalone, excellent as a ten-second beat inside a longer piece.

**"The stack it replaces."** Open on the real mess: WhatsApp threads, three spreadsheets, a bank statement PDF, a filing cabinet. Sweep it away into one screen. Classic problem/solution — resonates, but it's the most generic of the three.

**"Live in an afternoon."** Setup speed — sign up, add logo, first tenant onboarded. Good for reducing switching anxiety, which is your real competitor (inertia, not other software).

My instinct: month-end as the spine, with the brand-flip as a beat around the 30-second mark. And build it **caption-first** — the overwhelming majority of LinkedIn and WhatsApp viewing is muted, so the video has to work with the sound off, voiceover optional on top.

One caution on claims: with one agency live and no paying customers, everything must be product demonstration. No "trusted by", no invented numbers, no testimonials.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 11:41

Fair challenge — and thinking it through, I don't think I'd stand by it.

My reasoning was that a hero video is the most reusable single asset: it sits on the page permanently, works on every visitor, and you build it once. That logic holds for a site with traffic.

You don't have traffic yet. That's the whole reason we spent this afternoon on SEO and calculators. A hero video **converts** visitors; it doesn't **attract** them. Putting your first video where nobody currently looks is polishing an empty shop window.

There's also a technical tension I should have caught, since I created it: you went from a Speed Index of 33s to 4.7s and a Lighthouse score of 97. An autoplaying hero video is one of the most reliable ways to wreck LCP and undo that — and page speed is currently helping you rank, which is the thing actually feeding you visitors.

The better first video is the **15–20 second social cut**, because it travels. It can go on LinkedIn, in WhatsApp — which matters disproportionately in the SA market — in your partner recruitment pitch, and attached to sales replies. Distribution is the point; the video goes to people rather than waiting for them.

Second-best is the 90-second sales follow-up, because you have a real use for it right now: partner applicants and demo requests, where the viewer is already warm.

So the honest ordering is: social cut first, sales cut when you have conversations to send it into, hero video once traffic justifies it — and even then, as a click-to-play poster image rather than an autoplaying background, to protect Core Web Vitals.

If you're willing to do the capture work once, **"one script, three cuts"** is still the efficient path — you record the same footage and edit down. The 15s is what you actually publish first.

Which way do you want to go?

The production pack has the 90-second master script broken into seven beats with timecodes, the exact click path through your back-office for each shot, the caption copy, and the three cut-downs defined as timecode ranges of the same footage.

The cards file is a keyboard-driven recording stage — open in Chrome, F11, hit **1** for intro, **2** for outro, **3** for a lower third (**E** to edit its text for each caption you need). It renders on a fixed 1920×1080 stage scaled to your display, so framing is identical whatever monitor you record on.

Three things in there worth reading before you film:

**Seed a demo agency first.** Section 0. You'd otherwise be putting real tenant names, numbers and banking details into a public marketing asset — and doing it in a promo for POPIA-aligned software.

**Beat 4 is the film.** The payment landing and auto-reconciling into the double-entry ledger is the one thing no spreadsheet-and-hope competitor can show. I've noted to hold on it longer than feels natural.

**The 15-second cut is what you publish first.** The 45s hero waits until you have traffic, and when it lands it should be click-to-play, not autoplay — a background video would undo the Lighthouse 97 that's currently helping you rank.

Once you've got a rough cut, send me a frame or two and I'll give notes on pacing and caption legibility.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 12:01

Mostly yes — about 85% of it. Worth being precise about which parts.

**Automatable, properly:**

- **Demo data** — a seed script that creates the demo agency, fictional tenants, a lease and an unpaid invoice, deterministically. Rerun it and you get an identical starting state every time.
- **The capture** — Playwright drives Chromium through the exact click path and records 1080p video natively. You'd get one clip per beat, reproducible on demand.
- **The cursor** — Playwright's mouse is invisible in recordings, so you inject a synthetic cursor element and animate it with easing. Counter-intuitively this looks *better* than a human hand: perfectly smooth, consistent dwell times, no jitter.
- **Assembly** — ffmpeg concatenates the beats, burns in captions from a timings file, lays music underneath, and exports all three cuts plus the 1:1 and 9:16 social crops. One command.
- **The brand cards** — Playwright records those too; no manual keypresses needed.

**Not automatable, honestly:**

- Music selection and licence checking.
- The taste pass. First run will have pacing that's slightly off; you'll tune dwell times over two or three iterations.
- Voiceover, unless you pay for TTS — and for this market I'd still argue your own voice beats a synthetic American one.
- Phone footage, though Playwright's device emulation gets you a credible mobile viewport.

**The reason it's actually worth building** isn't this one video. It's two follow-on things:

1. **The video never goes stale.** You change the dashboard, you rerun the pipeline, the video matches the product again. Manual capture means the video quietly becomes a lie within three months.
2. **Personalised demos per prospect.** Since branding is already host-driven and parameterised, the same pipeline can generate a demo video showing *the prospect's own logo and colours* on the product. Sending an agency a 30-second video of their brand running on Locare is a materially stronger pitch than a generic one, and no competitor at your size will do it.

The catch: it runs where the app runs — your Windows machine against a local Docker stack, or the VPS against the demo agency. Not from here. And expect the first working version to take a couple of iterations before the pacing feels right.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 12:30

Three commands from empty database to finished video:

```bash
npm run seed
node scripts/video/record.mjs
bash scripts/video/assemble.sh
```

Out comes the 90s sales cut, 45s hero cut, 15s social cut, plus 1:1 and 9:16 crops.

**How it works.** `record.mjs` logs in through the passwordless flow — requests an OTP, scrapes `[OTP] … -> 123456` out of the API log, submits it — then drives each beat with a synthetic cursor injected into the page and eased with `easeInOutCubic`, since Playwright's real mouse doesn't appear in recordings. Clicks get a ripple. It genuinely looks smoother than hand-captured footage.

`assemble.sh` normalises Playwright's variable-framerate webm to uniform 1080p30, burns captions, concatenates each cut, lays music under at −18dB if you drop an mp3 in, and centre-crops the social versions.

**What I verified:** every ffmpeg filter chain, against synthetic clips that mimic Playwright's output — normalise, caption burn, concat, and both crops, confirming 1920×1080, 1080×1080 and 1080×1920 at 30fps. Shell syntax and the beats config parse clean.

**What I couldn't verify:** the selectors. There's no running stack here, so `text=Leases`, `text=Owners` and friends are educated guesses from your nav. A missing selector won't crash the run — the recorder warns, skips the click, and carries on — so run `DEBUG=1 node scripts/video/record.mjs` first and fix whatever it reports in `beats.config.mjs`. Expect two or three passes before the pacing feels right; each cycle is about two minutes.

Two things worth knowing: **never point this at production** (it films whatever's on screen, which against live data means real tenant details in a public asset), and the `BRANDS` block means you can generate a demo video showing a *prospect's own logo and colours* on the product — one command, and a materially better pitch than a generic reel.

`docs/video/raw/` and `out/` are gitignored so the binaries stay out of the repo.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 12:55

Both failures were prerequisites, not bugs — nothing was running and Playwright wasn't installed. I've also fixed a real design flaw the error exposed.

**Run this instead:**

```powershell
# once
npm i -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg     # reopen the terminal afterwards

# then
.\scripts\start-all.ps1 -Setup
node scripts/video/record.mjs
bash scripts/video/assemble.sh
```

`start-all.ps1 -Setup` brings up Docker (Postgres on 5433, Redis on 6380), applies migrations, seeds the Demo Agency and starts the API and web — which is what `npm run seed` was missing when it hit `ECONNREFUSED`.

**The design flaw:** I'd defaulted `OTP_CMD` to reading the *production* compose logs, which is wrong twice over — locally your API runs in its own PowerShell window, and I shouldn't be pointing a local tool at prod by default. Worse, I'd assumed the code could be recovered from somewhere; it can't. `otp_challenges` stores it hashed, so the console line is the only plaintext copy in existence.

So the recorder now pauses and asks:

```
Look in the API window for a line like:  [OTP] owner@demo.test -> 123456
Enter the code:
```

One prompt per run, then it's hands-off. Set `$env:OTP` beforehand to skip even that.

Expect the first run to report a few missing selectors — `text=Leases`, `text=Owners` and so on are guesses from your nav. It warns and carries on rather than dying, so you'll get clips either way; fix whatever it names in `beats.config.mjs` and go again.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 13:00

`start-all.ps1` does run `docker compose up -d`, but it doesn't check whether the command succeeded — so if Docker Desktop isn't running, it prints the message, fails silently, and marches on to start an API with no database. That's exactly what you're seeing.

First, check and start it:

```powershell
docker ps
```

If that errors with "cannot connect to the Docker daemon", **start Docker Desktop**, wait for the whale icon to settle, then:

```powershell
cd C:\xampp\htdocs\development\PMS0.3
docker compose up -d
docker ps        # expect pms-postgres-1 on 5433 and pms-redis-1 on 6380
```

Once both containers are listed, rerun `.\scripts\start-all.ps1 -Setup`.

Let me make the script fail loudly instead of limping on:

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 13:00

Docker Desktop isn't running — that's the whole cause. Both Postgres (5433) and Redis (6380) are containers, so nothing can connect until the daemon is up.

```powershell
docker ps
```

If that errors, start **Docker Desktop**, wait for the whale to settle, then:

```powershell
cd C:\xampp\htdocs\development\PMS0.3
.\scripts\start-all.ps1 -Setup
```

I've also fixed the script so this can't waste your time again. It now checks `docker info` before doing anything and stops with *"Docker isn't running — start Docker Desktop"* rather than pressing on to launch an API against a database that doesn't exist. It also waits for `pg_isready` before continuing, since Postgres accepts TCP connections a second or two before it can actually answer queries — which would otherwise make the migration or seed fail intermittently on a cold start.

      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public_listings(p_key text)
      RETURNS json
      LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public
      AS $$
        SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(row_to_json(x) ORDER BY x."availableFrom"), '[]'::json)
        FROM (
          SELECT l.id,
                 l.advertised_rent AS "rent",
                 l.available_from  AS "availableFrom",
                 l.description,
                 l.media,
                 u.label     AS "unitLabel",
                 u.bedrooms, u.bathrooms,
                 u.size_sqm AS "sizeSqm",
                 pr.name     AS "propertyName",
                 pr.address  AS "address",
                 pr.type     AS "propertyType"
          FROM listings l
          JOIN vendors v     ON v.id = l.vendor_id
          JOIN units u       ON u.id = l.unit_id
          JOIN properties pr ON pr.id = u.property_id
          WHERE l.status = 'published'
            AND v.status = 'active'
            AND (v.slug = p_key OR v.custom_domain = p_key)
        ) x;
      $$;
    
query: 
      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public_listing(p_id uuid)
      RETURNS json
      LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public
      AS $$
        SELECT row_to_json(x)
        FROM (
          SELECT l.id,
                 l.advertised_rent AS "rent",
                 l.available_from  AS "availableFrom",
                 l.description,
                 l.media,
                 u.label     AS "unitLabel",
                 u.bedrooms, u.bathrooms,
                 u.size_sqm AS "sizeSqm",
                 pr.name     AS "propertyName",
                 pr.address  AS "address",
                 pr.type     AS "propertyType",
                 v.name      AS "vendorName",
                 v.slug      AS "vendorSlug"
          FROM listings l
          JOIN vendors v     ON v.id = l.vendor_id
          JOIN units u       ON u.id = l.unit_id
          JOIN properties pr ON pr.id = u.property_id
          WHERE l.id = p_id AND l.status = 'published' AND v.status = 'active'
          LIMIT 1
        ) x;
      $$;

      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION partner_leaderboard()
      RETURNS json LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
        SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(row_to_json(x) ORDER BY x."referredMrr" DESC, x."agenciesSigned" DESC), '[]'::json)
        FROM (
          SELECT p.id AS "partnerId", p.name,
                 COALESCE(s.agencies, 0)   AS "agenciesSigned",
                 COALESCE(s.mrr, 0)        AS "referredMrr",
                 COALESCE(d.won, 0)        AS "dealsWon"
          FROM partners p
          LEFT JOIN (
            SELECT referred_by_partner_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS agencies, SUM(mrr) AS mrr
            FROM vendor_subscriptions
            WHERE referred_by_partner_id IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('active','trialing')
            GROUP BY referred_by_partner_id
          ) s ON s.pid = p.id
          LEFT JOIN (
            SELECT partner_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS won FROM partner_deals WHERE stage = 'won' GROUP BY partner_id
          ) d ON d.pid = p.id
          WHERE p.status = 'active'
        ) x;
      $$;
query: 
      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION provision_agency(
        p_partner uuid, p_agency text, p_slug text, p_owner_name text, p_owner_email text
      ) RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
      DECLARE v_vendor uuid; v_user uuid;
      BEGIN
        INSERT INTO vendors (name, slug, type, default_currency, status)
        VALUES (p_agency, NULLIF(p_slug,''), 'agency', 'ZAR', 'active')
        RETURNING id INTO v_vendor;
        INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (p_owner_name, p_owner_email)
        ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = COALESCE(users.name, EXCLUDED.name)
        RETURNING id INTO v_user;
        IF v_user IS NULL THEN SELECT id INTO v_user FROM users WHERE email = p_owner_email; END IF;
        INSERT INTO memberships (vendor_id, user_id, role, scope)
        VALUES (v_vendor, v_user, 'vendor_owner', '{}')
        ON CONFLICT (vendor_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;
        INSERT INTO vendor_subscriptions (vendor_id, tier, status, referred_by_partner_id)
        VALUES (v_vendor, 'starter', 'active', p_partner)
        ON CONFLICT (vendor_id) DO UPDATE SET referred_by_partner_id = EXCLUDED.referred_by_partner_id;
        RETURN v_vendor;
      END;
      $$;

query: 
      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION signup_agency(p_ref text, p_agency text, p_owner_name text, p_owner_email text)
      RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
      DECLARE v_partner uuid; v_vendor uuid; v_user uuid;
      BEGIN
        SELECT id INTO v_partner FROM partners WHERE ref_code = p_ref AND status = 'active';
        IF v_partner IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid or inactive referral code'; END IF;
        INSERT INTO vendors (name, type, default_currency, status)
        VALUES (p_agency, 'agency', 'ZAR', 'pending') RETURNING id INTO v_vendor;
        INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (p_owner_name, lower(p_owner_email))
        ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = COALESCE(users.name, EXCLUDED.name) RETURNING id INTO v_user;
        IF v_user IS NULL THEN SELECT id INTO v_user FROM users WHERE email = lower(p_owner_email); END IF;
        INSERT INTO memberships (vendor_id, user_id, role, scope)
        VALUES (v_vendor, v_user, 'vendor_owner', '{}') ON CONFLICT (vendor_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;
        INSERT INTO vendor_subscriptions (vendor_id, tier, status, referred_by_partner_id)
        VALUES (v_vendor, 'starter', 'pending', v_partner) ON CONFLICT (vendor_id) DO NOTHING;
        INSERT INTO partner_deals (partner_id, prospect_name, contact_email, stage, source, vendor_id, stage_changed_at)
        VALUES (v_partner, p_agency, lower(p_owner_email), 'proposal', 'referral_link', v_vendor, now());
        INSERT INTO partner_activities (partner_id, type, summary)
        VALUES (v_partner, 'signup', 'Referral signup: ' || p_agency);
        RETURN v_vendor;
      END; $$;
query: 
      CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION approve_agency(p_vendor uuid)
      RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
      BEGIN
        UPDATE vendor_subscriptions SET status = 'active', updated_at = now() WHERE vendor_id = p_vendor;
        UPDATE vendors SET status = 'active', updated_at = now() WHERE id = p_vendor;
        UPDATE partner_deals SET stage = 'won', stage_changed_at = now() WHERE vendor_id = p_vendor AND stage <> 'won';
      END; $$;

`w` is a keypress Expo listens for while Metro is running — not a command you type and press Enter on. And your prompt shows `PS C:\...\mobile-tenant>`, which means Metro has already exited in that window.

Just start it directly in web mode:

```powershell
cd C:\xampp\htdocs\development\PMS0.3\mobile-tenant
npx expo start --web
```

That skips the keypress and bundles the web build straight away. First bundle takes a minute or two; wait for `Web Bundled` and a browser tab on `http://localhost:8081`.

Once it's up, run the recorder from the repo root in a *separate* window:

```powershell
cd C:\xampp\htdocs\development\PMS0.3
node scripts/video/record.mjs
```

If Expo turns out to be a hassle, it's not a blocker — beat 4 is the only one that needs it. Set `TENANT_URL` to anything reachable, or delete that beat from `beats.config.mjs` and record the phone footage separately later. The other six beats are all back-office on port 3001.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-12 14:13

One command now:

```powershell
npm run video
```

It brings up Docker, waits for `pg_isready`, migrates, seeds the Demo Agency, starts the API, web and Expo web, polls each until it answers, records every beat, assembles the cuts, and kills what it started. About four minutes cold — most of that is Next and Expo compiling.

**The bit that makes it unattended** is the OTP. The API's stdout gets tee'd to `.video/api.log`, and the recorder polls that file for the `[OTP] owner@demo.test -> 123456` line matching the login email. That's the only way to automate a passwordless login here — `otp_challenges` stores the code hashed, so the console line is the sole plaintext copy. No auth weakening, no dev backdoor.

`scripts/video/video.config.json` holds everything tunable: URLs, login email, which services to start, wait timeouts, whether to reseed, whether to shut down afterwards. Environment variables override it.

Escape hatches for when a human's needed:

```powershell
npm run video -- -SkipRecord    # stack up, left running, fix selectors by hand
npm run video -- -KeepRunning   # don't tear down after
```

Two things I couldn't verify from here: the PowerShell orchestrator has never been executed (no Windows), and the selectors are still guesses. If `npm run video` falls over, the logs are in `.video/` — `api.log`, `web.log`, `tenant.log`, `migrate.log`, `seed.log` — and pasting the relevant one is the fastest route to a fix.

Only prerequisite it can't handle: Docker Desktop must already be running.

Secrets are clean — `.env` and `deploy/.env.prod` are gitignored and nothing sensitive is tracked. That simplifies things.

**What moves trivially.** The code isn't tied to any Claude account. It's on your disk and in `gunn3rfourlif3/PMS03`. The new account just needs folder access on whatever machine it runs on, or a clone. Everything I've written this session — design docs, the video pack, the WhatsApp setup guide, READMEs — lives in the repo and travels with it.

**What moves with a copy.** Your three scheduled tasks are plain files at `C:\Users\verno\Claude\Scheduled\` — `locare-monday-review`, `locare-partner-queue-sweep`, `locare-weekly-guide`. Each is a self-contained `SKILL.md`. Copy those folders to the same path under the new account's profile and they'll run. I deliberately wrote them self-contained, so they don't depend on this conversation.

**What doesn't move at all.** This conversation and everything in it — the reasoning behind decisions, the debugging history, why the brand resolution works the way it does, why the Custom tier sits in a band. Also the task list (#1–#223). Neither is exportable. A fresh account starts cold on a codebase with a lot of implicit context.

That's the real cost, and it's worth mitigating before you switch. A `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root capturing architecture, conventions, deploy commands and current gotchas would carry most of what matters. You don't have one — I checked earlier when looking for docs.

**The things that aren't Claude's at all** are the actual handover risk: VPS SSH access, the GitHub repo, HostAfrica DNS and mail, the Google Cloud OAuth project, Meta Business, iKhokha and the other gateway accounts. None of that is affected by which Claude account you use, but if "another account" means another *person*, that's the real checklist.

One trap worth flagging now: if you ever rotate `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, existing encrypted data becomes unreadable — owner banking details and partner KYC records are AES-256-GCM encrypted with it. Rotating it needs a decrypt-and-re-encrypt migration, not just a new value. `JWT_SECRET` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` rotate freely.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-08-13 08:31

`CLAUDE.md` is at the repo root — Claude reads it automatically in any session on this folder, so the new account starts knowing the architecture, the non-negotiables, the deploy commands, and every gotcha we paid for today rather than rediscovering them.

**The steps, for your own second account:**

1. **Commit the doc.**
   ```powershell
   git add CLAUDE.md scripts/video package.json .gitignore
   git commit -m "docs: CLAUDE.md handover notes + automated video pipeline"
   git push origin main
   ```

2. **Copy the scheduled tasks.** From `C:\Users\verno\Claude\Scheduled\` copy the three folders (`locare-monday-review`, `locare-partner-queue-sweep`, `locare-weekly-guide`) to the same path under whichever profile the new account runs as. They're self-contained `SKILL.md` files — no conversation dependency.

3. **Grant folder access.** Sign in on the new account and point Cowork at `C:\xampp\htdocs\development\PMS0.3` (and `EternalGuard` if you still want it).

4. **Leave the secrets alone.** `.env` and `deploy/.env.prod` stay on disk, gitignored and untracked. Same person, same machines, so nothing to rotate — and specifically **don't touch `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`**, or the encrypted owner banking and partner KYC records become unreadable.

**What you lose:** this conversation and the task list. Neither exports. `CLAUDE.md` carries the durable knowledge, but not the narrative — things like *why* the Custom pricing tier sits in a dark band, or that the branding bug looked like a caching problem for an hour before turning out to be static prerendering. If any of that matters, say so and I'll fold it in before you switch.

**What isn't affected at all:** VPS access, GitHub, DNS, Google Cloud, the gateway accounts. None of that knows or cares which Claude account you use.
